_what: Step b of the Commons' curation order: each college's local subject codes, from its printed catalog (kb/hand_filed_catalogs/courses/) beside the state list (coci_lookup_data.js). printed_name is the catalog's subject heading and the draft local subject title (owner: the Courses bot, state: drafted); null reads TBA. side says who prints the code: both, catalog (the catalog only) or state (the state list only). The codes on one side only are the curator's list. common is the common subject code (Step a) where the subject map and the canonical SUBJ give one. title_state says why a row has no title (not_read, blocked, not_in_catalog; catalog where it has one; a college whose file holds one section of its catalog, its index entry's scope, leaves the credit codes it never read not_read), title_source where the title came from, candidate a line for a reviewer where no heading was taken (never a title by itself), and address the subject's own page where the catalog's index links one (pages_not_read counts the linked pages that were not read; page_codes names the codes a page that was read prints its courses under, where that is not this code). A person's saved decision (kb/status/subject_decisions.json) replaces the title and the common code it names: title_state person, common_source person or statewide_filing (else subject_map), and decision names the save with what the files gave in was. renamed_to names the code a college renamed this one to, from its code history (kb/reference/subject_code_history/), which also titles it; history lists each change of code or title that names this code, with its source and who recorded it. Built by kb/_build_local_subject_titles.py; no clock is read, so read_at is each catalog's own.
_rule: A catalog's subject code and the state list's are the same code when they are equal after trimming and upper-casing; nothing looser. A college is the same college when its names are equal after lower-casing and folding every run of other characters to one space (Los Angeles Trade-Technical College is Los Angeles Trade Technical College). A local subject title is the catalog's subject heading, saved in Title Case, less a parenthetical that only repeats a subject code: the name its course pages carry, else the heading filed from the catalog's index or from the lines above the subject's first course (kb/hand_filed_catalogs/subjects/). A code the catalog's index lists is in the catalog whether or not its page's courses are filed. A row with no title says why (title_state): not_read where the catalog was not read for it, blocked where the reader was refused, not_in_catalog where the catalog was read and gives it none. credit_courses and noncredit_courses count the code's courses in the state list apart, and noncredit_plain and noncredit_enhanced split the noncredit ones by the state list's N and E. categories names the COCI noncredit categories of the code's noncredit courses, most courses first (kb/status/noncredit_categories.json). The common subject code is read from the subject map (its keys: upper case, letters and digits only) and the discipline's canonical SUBJ; where either has nothing, it is blank. A person's saved decision for the college's code and band wins over the catalog's heading and the subject map, and a person's statewide filing of the code in the Local subjects List wins over the map (kb/subject_decisions.py). A noncredit decision (band nc:<category>) touches the code's noncredit courses in that category only: noncredit_decisions lists each with whether the code still holds courses there, and a code whose courses are all noncredit takes its title from its dominant category's decision (another category's stands, marked moved) and its common code from the dominant category's decision. A TOP code is never read.
